span.p:
or: the paper really is missing —
add it in Zotero and re-sync

div.style: color: rgb(67, 20, 7) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center;

span.p:
0 · CURATE
you, in Zotero
Add papers, export
BibTeX + ☑ Export Files
papers/bibliography.bib
nothing else may invent a citekey

div.style: color: rgb(30, 27, 75) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center;

span.p:
1 · SYNC
job 1 — deterministic, no LLM
python -m src.sync
read bib → update ledger
→ extract PDF text
content/ledger.sqlite
content/parsed/*.txt
idempotent · re-runs cost almost nothing

div.style: color: rgb(5, 46, 22) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center;

span.p:
2 · DRAFT
job 2 — generative, you review
Ask a genre skill:
“write a survey section on …”
it retrieves only from
the parsed corpus
content/drafts/<slug>.md

div.style: color: rgb(69, 10, 10) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center;

span.p:
3 · VERIFY
machine-enforced
src.citation_gate
Is every citekey
in the ledger?

div.style: color: rgb(59, 7, 100) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center;

span.p:
4 · PUBLISH
stdlib + Pandoc / TeX Live
src.references
IEEE list from exactly
the citekeys cited
render_output --format pdf
content/rendered/<slug>.pdf

div.style: color: rgb(69, 10, 10) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center;

span.p:
DISCARD DRAFT
The skill throws the bad claim away
and drafts again — you never see this.
“Fix and re-run until OK.”
A FAIL is treated like a failing test,
not a lint warning.
